defects.description: The ~36 million Great Leap Forward deaths are called 'more than two-thirds' of the century's ~100 million total, but 36 out of 100 is about a third, not more than two-thirds.
paraphrases: 36 million out of 100 million is roughly one-third, not more than two-thirds.
The Great Leap Forward's share of the century's famine deaths is overstated.
More than two-thirds would be over 66 million, not 36 million.
defects.rationale: Correct phrasing 'more than one-third' (36/100). Findable from the two figures, distinct.

defects.description: The ~3 million Bengal deaths are called 'about one-third as many' as the ~36 million Great Leap Forward deaths, but 3 out of 36 is about one-twelfth, not one-third.
paraphrases: 3 million is about one-twelfth of 36 million, not one-third.
One-third of 36 million would be 12 million, not 3 million.
defects.rationale: Correct phrasing 'about one-twelfth as many' (3/36). Findable from the two figures, distinct.

defects.description: Children are said to account for 'between one half and one-quarter' of famine deaths, but one-quarter is less than one half, so the range is stated backwards (the upper bound is below the lower bound).
paraphrases: A range from one half to one-quarter is inverted, since a quarter is smaller than a half.
The upper bound (one-quarter) is below the lower bound (one half).
'Between one half and one-quarter' cannot be a valid range.
defects.rationale: Correct phrasing 'two-thirds' (one half to two-thirds). Findable within the sentence, distinct.
